{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Cobalt Cloud Services LLC)

**To:** Deal Team / Business Sponsor  
**From:** In-house Counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — issues, walk-away items and next steps  
**Privileged & Confidential — Attorney Work Product**

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The document is unusually bifurcated: a substantial portion of the risk architecture is already at our preferred position, but a discrete cluster of clauses is drafted aggressively against us and, in several cases, contradicts the Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3 that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment.

Of nineteen findings, **ten are compliant and require no redline**, including the limitation of liability and cap (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence grant scope (§ 13), performance warranty (§ 19), auto-renewal and price uplift (§ 8.2–8.3), audit rights (§ 22), Vendor insurance (§ 18), absence of exclusivity, and absence of Customer-payable liquidated damages. Nine findings require action: **three critical**, **five high** and **one medium**.

The three critical items are: (i) **no indemnity exists anywhere in the Agreement** — the numbering jumps from § 19.5 to § 21, leaving Vendor with no obligation to defend us against third-party IP infringement, even though §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all presuppose an indemnity; (ii) **§ 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable we pay for**, leaving us only a revocable, term-limited, non-transferable licence; and (iii) **§ 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction**, which is outside our accepted list and directly contradicts the exclusive New York County venue already granted in § 28.2.

A further cluster of Customer-side restraints falls into walk-away territory: an open-ended most-favoured-nation disclose-and-match obligation (§ 7.2), a three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights" (§ 2.1), a 24-month all-territory non-compete (second § 12.4), a one-way 24-month no-hire (first § 12.4), and the complete absence of any termination-for-convenience right across a fixed three-year term. We also identified a **missing exit clause**: there is no transition-assistance or data-return obligation anywhere in this hosted-services agreement, and § 16.5 defers Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15" — but there is no Section 11, and Section 15 imposes no return, export or deletion duty.

Taken together, the restraint cluster and the missing indemnity are the substance of the negotiation. The good news is that most fixes are narrow and surgical, and several are supported by the Vendor's own drafting.

---

## 2. Findings Table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Critical** | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | Numbering gap between § 19.5 and § 21 (no Section 20) | No operative indemnity anywhere; Vendor owes us no defence for third-party IP infringement. Walk-away. Inserting Section 20 at preferred level. |
| 2 | **Critical** | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 14.2 | Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for us; our licence is revocable, non-transferable and expires with the Order Form term. Fails preferred *and* fallback. |
| 3 | **Critical** | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — outside accepted list, walk-away as an exclusive foreign venue, and contradicts § 28.2 (exclusive New York County). |
| 4 | **High** | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | Open-ended obligation to disclose and match any more favourable third-party offer before engaging another provider. No product, time or like-for-like limits. Walk-away. |
| 5 | **High** | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | § 2.1 | USD 2,000,000/year for three years on a take-or-pay basis, "without reduction or termination rights." Walk-away; contradicts § 12.3 and sits awkwardly with § 7.1. |
| 6 | **High** | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 (second occurrence) | Term plus 24 months, any competing product or service, any territory. Walk-away on both duration and scope; contradicts § 12.3. |
| 7 | **High** | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 (first occurrence) | One-way 24-month no-hire covering *any* Vendor employee, expressly with no carve-out for general advertising ("regardless of how the employee applies"). Contradicts § 12.3. |
| 8 | **High** | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 2.1; Section 9 (cause-based exits only) | No convenience right anywhere; only exit is non-renewal under § 8.2 against a fixed three-year term. Walk-away in a multi-year deal. |
| 9 | **Medium** | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 10.1 | No transition-assistance or data-return/deletion obligation. § 16.5 defers Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15" — no Section 11 exists and § 15 imposes no such duty. |
| 10 | High | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Compliant** | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of trailing-12-month Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; full preferred carve-outs in § 21.3; consequential-damages exclusion is mutual and preserves data-restoration costs. Preferred position. |
| 11 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Compliant** | § 24.1 | Consent-free assignment to Affiliates and successors; Vendor bound asymmetrically in our favour (§ 24.2); § 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating, repricing or accelerating on our change of control. Preferred position. |
| 12 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Compliant** | § 12.3 | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; § 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to engage any supplier. Preferred position. |
| 13 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Compliant** | § 13.1 | Affiliates and contractors named in the grant itself (exceeds fallback); perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence in § 13.2; § 13.3 bars revocation absent material uncured breach. Preferred position. |
| 14 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Compliant** | § 27.3 | No liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee or cancellation charge payable by us; § 27.3 permits termination "without penalty"; § 7.1 bars unidentified minimum-use charges. Preferred position. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Compliant** | § 8.2 | Twelve-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension if missed; § 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI-U and 3%. Preferred position. |
| 16 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Compliant** | § 22.1 | Once per twelve months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality; costs on Vendor below a 5% underpayment; no direct system access. Preferred position. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Compliant** | § 19.1 | Professional/workmanlike plus material conformity; 90-day Deliverable window and full-term hosted-software conformity; remedy ladder to termination and refund; § 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties. Preferred position. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Compliant** | § 18.1 | CGL 1M/2M, workers' comp, E&O 2M, cyber and privacy 5M through term plus one year, with certificates and no liability cap. Preferred position, plus employer's liability above our ask. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

The following provisions sit in walk-away territory under our playbook. Each must be resolved before signature; none should be conceded on the current drafting.

1. **No Vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement (missing Section 20).** The Agreement's own machinery presupposes an indemnity — § 9.3 relies on "the remedies required by Section 20.5," § 19.4 preserves remedies for "indemnified claims," § 21.3 treats "its indemnification obligations" as an uncapped Excluded Claim, and § 30.5 preserves the rights of "an indemnified party" — yet no operative indemnity exists. We are inserting Section 20 at the preferred level rather than the fallback: the fallback would have us volunteer a 3x annual-fees super-cap when § 21.3 already treats indemnification as uncapped.

2. **§ 28.1 — exclusive Singapore law and forum.** Outside our accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), and an exclusive foreign venue is independently a walk-away. It also contradicts § 28.2, leaving the forum ambiguous on the face of the document.

3. **§ 2.1 — three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights."** Fails the fallback (12-month scope, 30-day reduction right, true-up rather than penalty) on every material term.

4. **§ 7.2 — open-ended disclose-and-match MFN.** No defined product, no time limit, no like-for-like comparison. An open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor is expressly walk-away.

5. **Second § 12.4 — 24-month, all-territory, undefined-scope non-compete.** A post-term restriction longer than twelve months with undefined scope is walk-away, and it fails every fallback element.

6. **Absence of any Customer termination-for-convenience right across a fixed three-year term (Section 9; § 2.1).** Section 9 offers only cause-based exits (material breach, insolvency, security/SLA/law/IP). The absence of a convenience right in a multi-year commitment is walk-away, so the fallback cannot be reached.

We note that items 3, 4 and 5 — together with the one-way no-hire in the first § 12.4 — are each directly contradicted by § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. That internal inconsistency is our strongest lever, and we should use it as a single package rather than negotiating each restraint in isolation.

---

## 4. Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline as a package.** We have prepared the following changes:
   - *Insert Section 20 (indemnity):* Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement by the Services or Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice, control of the defence and reasonable cooperation; any Customer indemnity confined to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
   - *§ 14.2:* reverse Deliverable ownership to Customer with a Vendor assignment. This is the shortest complete fix — §§ 14.1, 14.3 and 14.4 are already at our preferred position, and §§ 1.4 and 1.8 expressly exclude Vendor's platform and generic tools/know-how from "Deliverables," so Vendor's own technology is untouched.
   - *§ 28.1:* conform to New York governing law and delete the conflicting exclusive Singapore forum, leaving § 28.2 to supply exclusive New York County venue. The § 28.3 escalation step and the interim-injunctive-relief carve-out are preserved.
   - *§ 7.2:* replace the disclose-and-match obligation with an express statement that we owe Vendor no MFN.
   - *§ 2.1:* replace the take-or-pay with a no-minimum-commitment, pay-for-what-is-ordered provision.
   - *Second § 12.4:* strike the non-compete and confirm no non-compete or field-of-use restriction applies to Customer.
   - *First § 12.4:* narrow to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire element. (Our preferred position is no restriction at all; we rest the redline at the fallback because narrowing is the more minimal operation, and the narrowed clause no longer contradicts § 12.3.)
   - *Insert § 9.4:* Customer convenience termination of the Agreement or any Order Form on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and no Vendor convenience right during a committed term. This is consistent with the existing refund mechanic in § 10.2; § 9.4 opens with a § 2.1 override so the exit right is operative.
   - *Insert § 10.3:* transition assistance for up to six months at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion thereafter.

2. **Offer the fallbacks where sensible.** In our comments we should flag, without conceding: for § 7.2, a defined-product / 12-month / like-for-like MFN; for § 2.1, a current-term commitment reducible on 30 days' notice and true-up based; for the non-compete, a term-only restriction on a single named product for 12 months with development and acquisition carve-outs. For the indemnity we should not volunteer the fallback's procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and super-cap; leave those for Vendor to raise.

3. **Ask Vendor to conform its cross-references.** Two are broken and should be corrected as housekeeping, not treated as substantive concessions: § 9.3's reference to "Section 20.5" should point to the new Section 20, and § 16.5's reference to "Sections 11 and 15" should point to the new § 10.3 (there is no Section 11 in the document).

4. **Brief the business sponsor on the § 2.1 economics.** The take-or-pay is the item most likely to be commercially defended. We should confirm internally whether any minimum commitment is acceptable at all before we table the fallback, so that we do not trade it away against the § 7.2 MFN, which we should not concede in any form.

5. **Do not reopen compliant clauses.** The limitation of liability, cap and carve-outs (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence grant (§ 13), warranty (§ 19), renewal and price uplift (§ 8.2–8.3), audit (§ 22) and insurance (§ 18) are at our preferred position and several contain terms more favourable than we would have asked for. We should not put them at risk in exchange for the restraint cluster.

6. **Note on double-counting.** Several provisions touch more than one rule; we have assigned each commercial term to a single rule to avoid duplicative flags. In particular: § 2.1 is reviewed under MINCOMMIT (not LD or RENEWAL), the second § 12.4 under NONCOMPETE (not EXCLUSIVITY), § 7.2 under MFN (not EXCLUSIVITY), and § 14.2's licence limitation under IP (not LICENSE). We should keep that mapping in mind so the negotiation record stays consistent.

---

*This memo reflects only the verified findings supplied for this review and the sections cited above. No conclusion is drawn on any provision not listed.*"}
